newsitem.title: NORWAY: Japan, Nordic states hold first summit.
newsitem.headline: Japan, Nordic states hold first summit.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and the five Nordic premiers held the first Nordic-Japanese summit on Thursday, covering a discussion agenda that ranged from Russia and China to global warming.
Both sides agreed they would like this first meeting to be the start of a regular gathering.

"On the Nordic side we have Japan as our most important political and trading partner in Asia," Norwegian Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland told a news conference after the talks in this picturesque western Norwegian city.
As well as Jagland, Hashimoto met Denmark's Poul Nyrup Rasmussen, Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson, Icelandic leader David Oddsson and Finnish premier Paavo Lipponen.
Jagland said the six leaders expressed their desire to boost cooperation, including an interest in ties with Russia.
Reforms of the United Nations, the environment and social welfare were also on the agenda.
"My Nordic colleagues explained that cooperation with Russia and the Baltic states was progressing," Hashimoto said.
He told the Nordic leaders that China's position should be "cemented" positively in the world.
Hashimoto said that the Nordics and Japan would like to continue cooperation through many channels and that further summits should take place.

Much emphasis was also placed on environmental issues, with both sides saying that a concrete agreement on reducing the global output of greenhouse gases must be reached at a conference in the Japanese city of Kyoto in December.
Hashimoto has sought to play the role of mediator in finding agreement on targets for legally binding cuts in heat-trapping pollution at the conference.
"I believe it is neccessary to bring that conference to a successful conclusion...we have to come up with a Kyoto protocol," Hashimoto said.
"Now is the time for action," Denmark's Rasmussen said. "We have to make a decision in Kyoto."
Jagland said the Nordic states and Japan had different strategies but shared the aim of getting an ambitious climate agreement.
